names.name: the soul's own nature (svabhāva) with its infinite fourfold

descriptions: Each soul's own pure nature: infinite knowledge, perception, bliss and energy, manifest when all karma is shed (TS 10.2–4).
The liberated soul abides at the summit of the universe, bodiless, knowing all substances and all modes (TS 1.29, 10.5).
Called by others Sadāśiva, the supreme Brahman, the perfected self, suchness — one goal under many names (Haribhadra, YDS 129–130).
Non-violence is called the supreme Brahman known in the world (Svayambhūstotra, recalled).
negations: No creator or controller of the world (Ādipurāṇa 4; Anyayogavyavacchedikā 6).
Not one all-pervading self: souls are innumerable, distinct and body-sized (TS 5.16).
Not merely permanent nor merely momentary (TS 5.30).
relation_to_self: The ultimate is the soul's own nature, realised by each soul for itself through the three jewels; the Jina is the model, not the giver.
relation_to_world: The world of six eternal substances is real and uncreated; the liberated soul knows it wholly but does not act on it.
caveat: Jainism denies a single ultimate being: the liberated are infinitely many individual souls, alike in nature but not one. In Jain terms 'all is one' is the collective standpoint (saṃgraha-naya), true of things only in respect of their common character 'existence', and false when made absolute (the Jain reading of Vedāntic monism). A reading of 'ekaṃ sat' as one reality would be accepted only in that limited standpoint; Haribhadra's 'one goal, many names' concerns the one state of liberation, not one soul.
notes: U35 contribution (lin:jainism is owned by U34, which may add its own view under the same id; the merge unions them).

descriptions: The self shining by self-experience, whose nature is consciousness, cutting through all other states (Samayasāra-kalaśa 1).
One, pure, made of perception and knowledge, formless; not even an atom of anything else is mine (Samayasāra 38).
Who the supreme self is, that am I (Yogīndu, Yogasāra 22).
negations: Not the body, not karma, not the passions (Iṣṭopadeśa 50).
Not the doer of material karma in the ultimate standpoint.
relation_to_self: Identical with one's own pure self as seen by the ultimate standpoint; realised through discriminative knowledge and self-experience.
relation_to_world: The world of substances is real; the self is its knower, not its maker; conventional conduct belongs to the path, not to the self's nature.
caveat: 'I am the supreme self' in the Adhyātma texts means that each soul's own nature is the perfected state, not that all souls are one Brahman; the movement accepts the Jain plurality of souls and the reality of the world, and its mature form insists on holding the conventional standpoint alongside the ultimate.
